claims.text: Narrowly tuning Al content in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni governs phase stability by inducing an FCC γ plus ordered γ′ dual-phase microstructure.
Al promotes the formation of thermodynamically stable Al2O3 together with Cr2O3 at internal and external surfaces.
The combined γ/γ′ microstructure and Al/Cr oxide scales underpin simultaneous high-temperature strength, oxidation resistance, radiation resistance, and cryogenic toughness.
An equiatomic or near-equiatomic Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni baseline is predominantly FCC γ with possible minor ordering.
The controlled comparison varies Al in small increments around an optimum while holding the Co:Cr:Fe:Ni proportions and processing conditions fixed.
Al content controls the formation, size distribution, and volume fraction of ordered γ′ precipitates in the FCC matrix.
Al content controls the development of protective Al2O3/Cr2O3 oxide scales.
An optimal Al amount enhances chemical ordering in the FCC matrix and precipitates fine γ′ particles.
Fine γ′ precipitates provide high-temperature strength and thermal stability.
The chemical affinity of Al, aided by Cr, produces thermodynamically stable oxide scales.
The stable Al/Cr oxide scales suppress oxidation.
The stable oxide scales suppress radiation-induced defect evolution.
Al-induced changes in stacking-fault energy promote twinning or related deformation mechanisms that improve cryogenic toughness.
The optimal-Al alloy will have higher high-temperature strength than the baseline and off-optimum alloys.
The optimal-Al alloy will have greater oxidation resistance than the baseline and off-optimum alloys.
The optimal-Al alloy will have greater radiation resistance than the baseline and off-optimum alloys.
The optimal-Al alloy will have greater cryogenic fracture toughness than the baseline and off-optimum alloys.
The hypothesis is limited to near-equiatomic Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni and excludes large Al deviations or additional alloying elements.
The exact optimal Al window and the relative contributions of γ′ precipitation and oxide formation remain undetermined.
